Subject: Production reliability ask & commercial constraints

Laura —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We had an internal readout and the execs are generally impressed with the latency numbers, but our finance team is pushing back on the enterprise package price. Two asks from my side so we can move faster: 1) a small concession on monthly rate for first 12 months, and 2) permission for a slightly lower uptime commitment (we can accept 99.5% instead of the standard 99.9%) so we can hit price targets.

We know lower uptime usually means higher credits; can Redwood consider capping service credits at 10% of monthly bill for the first year if we sign the 12-month commitment? If you can provide a written proposal I can escalate internally. Attaching our requested terms.

—Eric

Team — forwarding Medley’s ask (attached). Quick summary: 1) Customer is asking to accept 99.5% uptime in contract instead of our standard 99.9%. 2) They request a hard cap on service credits at 10% of monthly invoice for year 1. ARR upside: $275k ARR if we convert; immediate ARR run-rate for first year estimated at $220k.

Why I recommend we escalate: Medley is in active pilots with a competing vendor; they’ve asked for written confirmation by Friday (2026-08-09). If we push back to standard SLA/credit terms they will push to competitor. Risk is manageable given their traffic profile (pre-prod-ish batch patterns) — support estimates minimal continuous failure exposure.

Requested approvals / decisions:
- Approve temporary contract deviation: uptime target = 99.5% for the first 12 months (then revert to 99.9%)
- Cap total service credits at 10% of monthly charges for months 1–12
- Approve a one-time commercial concession: 8% discount on TCV (handled by Deal Desk) if legal signs off on the credit cap language

Reasoning / mitigations:
- We will require monitored KPIs, weekly health check calls for first 90 days, and automatic escalation to Redwood L3 on any >=30 minute outage affecting >10% of their traffic.
- We can include a sunset clause: exception expires at month 12, with the option to renegotiate at renewal but defaulting back to standard SLA.

Attachments: deal-summary-aug-2026.xlsx (traffic and revenue model)

Action: Aditya, please confirm commercial levers and final discount; Marissa, please advise on redline language to enforce cap and sunset; Dylan/Rohan, will Deal Desk need any additional bookkeeping or approval routing? Hannah — please confirm support/resources for 90-day accelerated onboarding.

Thanks —Laura
Laura Bennett

Laura / Aditya — I reviewed Medley’s request and drafted a redline (attached: legal-redline-sla.docx). Key points included in the redline:

1) Exception clause: "Temporary Uptime Deviation" — explicitly states a one-year deviation to 99.5% and reversion to default 99.9% unless both parties agree in writing otherwise.
2) Credit cap: service credit liability for months 1–12 shall be capped at the lesser of (i) 10% of the monthly invoice; or (ii) $75,000 per calendar month — legal wants a numeric ceiling to limit open-ended exposure.
3) Monitoring / remediation commitments: customer-facing weekly health calls for first 90 days; Redwood will provide an L3 contact and 4-hour incident response SLA for Sev1 affecting >10% of traffic.
4) Audit and proof: customer must provide usage logs and reproduce incident windows for credits to be payable.

Open asks for Execs:
- Approve the numeric ceiling on credits ($75k) OR propose a different limit.
- Confirm approval to include the sunset clause (automated reversion).

If the execs sign off, I’ll prepare the final contract package and mark the clause as "Deal Desk Exception — Exec Approved".

—Marissa
